chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whatever affliction befalls you, it is on account of what your hands have wrought, and what He Pardons is more'
'There is none from the twisting of a vein, nor a stumbling over a stone, nor a slip of a foot, nor a scratch by wood, except it is due to a sin,'

So for the one for whom Allah Hastens the Punishment for his sin in the world, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more Majestic and more Benevolent and more Magnificent than for Him to Repeat Punishing him in the Hereafter.

key_terms.فَبِما كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ: on account of what your hands have wrought
key_terms.وَيَعْفُوا عَنْ كَثِيرٍ: and what He Pardons is more

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of hastened punishment in this world according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'Tasri' (hastening punishment), where minor worldly afflictions serve as expiation for sins, sparing the believer from retribution in the Hereafter. It highlights Allah’s magnanimity in choosing to settle accounts in this transient life rather than accumulating debt for the eternal realm, a key theme in Shia theology regarding divine justice and mercy.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [42:30] And whatever affliction befalls you, it is on account of what your hands have wrought, and what He Pardons is more: ‘There is none from the twisting of a vein (muscle), nor a stumbling over a stone, nor a slip of a foot, nor a scratch by wood, except it is due to a sin, and what Heazwj Pardons is more.

So for the one for whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Hastens the Punishment for his sin in the world, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is more Majestic and more Benevolent and more Magnificent than for Him<sup>azwj</sup> to Repeat Punishing him in the Hereafter’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from Misma’ ibn ‘Abd al-Malik from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘Whatever hardship befalls you is the result of your own deeds. Allah pardons many of your sins,’ [42:30] has said, ‘The spraining of one’s muscles, bumping over a stone, the slip of foot or being bruised by a piece of wood is all because of sins
what Allah forgives is much more.

In the matters of whoever faces quick suffering for sins in this world, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, is by far more Honorable and Great and will not allow a repeat of his suffering in the next life.”’
